title: Video streaming player (Netflix / YouTube style)
summary: Adaptive streaming with HLS, fast start, resume across devices, offline downloads with DRM, and a player architecture that is testable and measurable (startup time, rebuffering ratio).
requirements: Play on-demand video with adaptive bitrate; start in under 2s; minimal rebuffering.
Resume position across devices; subtitles, audio tracks, Picture in Picture, AirPlay.
Download for offline with DRM and expiry.
components: Backend: transcoding into an HLS bitrate ladder, CDN, manifest service, DRM license server (FairPlay)
Player layer: AVPlayer + AVPlayerItem, a PlayerController state machine, UI separate from playback logic
Playback session service: progress heartbeats every N seconds, resume position, concurrent stream limits
Download manager: `AVAssetDownloadURLSession` for HLS offline, persistent FairPlay keys
QoE telemetry: startup time, rebuffer count/duration, bitrate switches, errors
tradeoffs: Lower starting bitrate starts faster but looks worse at first; use network estimates to pick.
Larger forward buffer reduces rebuffering but wastes data if users abandon.
Preloading the next episode/feed video improves start time at a data cost.
body: **Fast start:** prefetch manifest and first segments for likely-next content, reuse a warmed AVPlayer, set `preferredForwardBufferDuration`, and show the poster frame immediately.
**Feed autoplay (short video):** a small pool of players, play only the most visible cell, preload the next 1-2 items, muted by default; release players aggressively to cap memory.
**State machine:** idle → loading → readyToPlay → playing ⇄ paused/buffering → ended/failed; observe `timeControlStatus`, `status` and item notifications; expose as an async stream to the UI.
**Offline:** download the chosen rendition and subtitles; store persistent content keys; enforce license expiry; clean up when storage is low.
**Metrics:** video start time p50/p95, rebuffering ratio, playback failure rate, average bitrate by network.
